title: Wren's Croft
shortDescription: A peat fire, a kettle, and one empty peg.
longDescription:
The croft is low stone and wet thatch. A peat fire keeps the kettle honest. Two cloaks drip by the door; a third peg is empty where a crook should hang.
Oatcakes wait on a tin plate, still warm. Shepherd Wren does not pretend this is a lesson she wanted.

fixtures.name: Shepherd Wren
fixtures.lookDescription: An adult hare in a wet cloak, peat-smoke in her fur, kettle-calluses on both paws. Try talk wren.
fixtures.examineDescription: Wren's ears are notched from weather, not from practice. Her cloak is mended with wool. She keeps glancing at the doorway while she talks to you, and she has not sat down once since you came in. She is frightened, and she is not hiding it well.
fixtures.dialogue: Wren has the kettle on and has not sat down since you came in. "Sit, if you like. I cannot." She glances at the door again. "Colm has not come in. The flock was due at dusk yesterday and his peg is empty. Eat something warm before you go naming anything you saw in the mist. Talk wren when you are ready."

welcome.text: "I am Wren. Sit. The kettle is on, and the oatcakes are still warm enough to matter. Colm has not come in. The flock was due at dusk yesterday, and the peg where his crook should hang is empty. An empty peg is not proof of anything walking. Eat. Then examine the waystone on the track south of here. Come back and talk wren. Alder sent you? Good. Whatever is out on that moor, it is not the queen again."

colm.text: "My partner. He counts sheep twice and writes the number down, the same way Alder does with facts. He went out to look at standing stones that were not in last winter's count. I told him not to go. Eat something. Then go and look. I am owed the truth, not a kind version of it."

go.text: "South to the waystone. Examine it. Then talk wren here. The oatcakes will keep. I will not."

fork-done.text: "The waystone told you the same three counts the chapel knows. East is the fold. The latch was lifted, not broken. Examine the empty fold and Colm's crook. There has been a mist-crow on that rail three days running and it has worn the moss off the top of it. Defeat it if it squares up. Then talk wren. I will have the kettle too hot by then."

flock-done.text: "The stones next. They were not in last winter's count. Colm went to look. I told him not to. East from the fold. Examine the abbey mark and the new stone. Then talk wren. I will not go with you. Someone has to keep the kettle."

stones-done.text: "Last winter there were seven. There are eight. North of the stones the peat-cut opens, then the barrow mouth. I hate sending you. If you find him, you come to me before you go to Alder. I am owed that. Examine the wool wrap. The barrow-guard is peat-and-bone that is not a dog. Then talk wren."

barrow-done.text: "You found the spare cloak. Now the lip of the barrow. Examine what the fog took. Then come to me. Do not go to Alder first. I asked you that already."

after-colm.text: "Put the kettle down. I put it down too hard. Did you tell him anything? No. Do not answer that. I hate the question. Go to Fen. Sit. Honey. Tell him if you can feel your paws. I will keep this fire. I will not go into the hill."

stay.text: "Alder can have the bronze. I will not go in. The kettle is for the living. If the fog squares up, you lock together. Then Fen. Then you come back here and eat."

tally-page.text: Wren reads Kern's page twice and then puts the kettle down without pouring anything. "Hobb's bell. Sile's mere. Kern's stone. Three animals who count things properly, all wrong in the same week, and none of them came to me." She hands the page back and does not soften it. "That is not comfort and I will not pretend it is. Take it up to Alder. He is owed facts as much as I am, and he is the one who can do something with a date."

fixtures.name: Empty Peg
fixtures.lookDescription: A peg by the door with no crook on it. Examine it.
fixtures.examineDescription: Wool fibres still cling to the wood. The peg is not broken. Someone took a crook down carefully and meant to hang it back. They have not.
